{{Short description|None}}
A [[mathematical constant]] is a key [[number]] whose value is fixed by an unambiguous definition, often referred to by a symbol (e.g., an [[Letter (alphabet)|alphabet letter]]), or by mathematicians' names to facilitate using it across multiple [[mathematical problem]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Weisstein|first=Eric W.|title=Constant|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Constant.html|access-date=2020-08-08|website=mathworld.wolfram.com|language=en}}</ref> For example, the constant [[Pi|π]] may be defined as the ratio of the length of a circle's [[circumference]] to its [[diameter]]. The following list includes a [[decimal expansion]] and set containing each number, ordered by year of discovery.

The column headings may be clicked to sort the table alphabetically, by decimal value, or by set. Explanations of the symbols in the right hand column can be found by clicking on them.

== Mathematical constants sorted by their representations as continued fractions ==
The following list includes the [[continued fraction]]s of some constants and is sorted by their representations. Continued fractions with more than 20 known terms have been truncated, with an [[ellipsis]] to show that they continue. Rational numbers have two continued fractions; the version in this list is the shorter one. Decimal representations are [[rounding|rounded]] or padded to 10 places if the values are known.

|[[Lagrange number]]
|<math>L(n)</math>
|<math>\sqrt{9-\frac{4}{{m_n}^2}}</math> where <math>m_n</math> is the nth smallest number such that <math>m^2+x^2+y^2=3mxy\,</math> has positive (x,y)
| data-sort-value="1957"|before 1957
| data-sort-value="4" |[[Algebraic number|<math>\mathbb{A}</math>]]
|-
|[[Feller's coin-tossing constants]]
|<math>\alpha_k,\beta_k</math>
|<math>\alpha_k</math> is the smallest positive real root of <math>x^{k+1}=2^{k+1}(x-1),\beta_k=\frac{2-\alpha_k}{k+1-k\alpha_k}</math>
| 1968
| data-sort-value="4" |[[Algebraic number|<math>\mathbb{A}</math>]]
|-
|[[Stoneham number]]
|<math>\alpha_{b,c}</math>
|<math>\sum_{n=c^k>1} \frac{1}{b^nn} = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{b^{c^k}c^k}</math> where ''b'',''c'' are coprime integers
| 1973
| data-sort-value="6" |[[Transcendental number|<math>\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{A}</math>]]
|-
|[[Beraha constants]]
|<math>B(n)</math>
|<math>2+2\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{n}\right)</math>
| 1974
| data-sort-value="7" |[[Real number|<math>\mathbb{A}</math>]]
|-
|[[Chvátal–Sankoff constants]]
|<math>\gamma_k</math>
|<math>\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{E[\lambda_{n,k}]}{n}</math>
| 1975
| data-sort-value="7" |[[Real number|<math>\mathbb{R}</math>]]
|-
|[[Hyperharmonic number]]
|<math>H^{(r)}_n</math>
|<math>\sum^n_{k=1}H^{(r-1)}_k</math> and <math>H^{(0)}_n=\frac{1}{n}</math>
| 1995
|data-sort-value="3" |[[Rational number|<math>\mathbb{Q}</math>]]
|-
|[[Gregory number]]
|<math>G_x</math>
|<math>\sum _{n=0}^{\infty }(-1)^{n}{\frac {1}{(2n+1)x^{2n+1}}}=\arccot(x)</math> for rational x greater than or equal to one
| data-sort-value="1996"|before 1996
| data-sort-value="7" |[[Transcendental number|<math>\mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{A}</math>]]
|-
|[[Metallic mean]]
|
|<math>\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}</math>
|data-sort-value="1998" | before 1998
|data-sort-value="4" |[[Algebraic number|<math>\mathbb{A}</math>]]
|}
